kit.title: Multilingual Service Flyer Translation Check Kit
kit.summary: Checks each translated service flyer against its English source for dropped facts, changed numbers, dates and phone numbers, untranslated text and reading level. A fluent community reviewer approves each language, and staff decide what gets printed and posted.
kit.target_org: Community health and services center printing flyers in five languages

steps.title: Compare facts across the source and each translation
steps.guidance: List every fact in the English source, such as the service, hours, dates, address line, phone number, cost and who can use it, and check that each appears unchanged in each translation. Numbers, dates and phone numbers must match exactly.

steps.title: Draft questions for the fluent reviewer
steps.guidance: For each language, list the sentences where meaning may have shifted, words left in English and sentences above the target reading level, as questions for the fluent reviewer, not corrections.

steps.title: Approve each translation (fluent community reviewer)
steps.guidance: A fluent speaker from the community reads the whole flyer, answers the questions and approves or corrects the translation. Machine checks never replace this step.

steps.title: Decide what gets printed and posted
steps.guidance: Staff print and post only translations the fluent reviewer approved, and keep each approval with its flyer version.

skills.name: flyer-fact-checker
skills.description: Compares a translated flyer with its English source for dropped or changed facts, exact numbers and dates, and untranslated text.
skills.instructions: Work from the English source and the translation the center provides. Build a fact list from the source: service name, days, hours, dates, address line, phone number, cost and who can use the service. For each translation, mark each fact as matching, changed or missing; numbers, dates, times and phone numbers must match character for character after normal formatting for that language. List words left in English. Turn every problem into a question for the fluent reviewer. Never rewrite the translation yourself and never call a translation approved.
refuses: Approving a translation
Rewriting a flyer in another language for printing
Printing, posting or sharing a flyer
Guessing a fact the source does not state

tools.name: compare_flyer_facts
tools.description: Extracts dates, times, phone numbers and amounts from the source and each translation and lists any that differ or are missing.

artifacts.name: translation_review_sheet
artifacts.title: Translation Review Sheet
artifacts.summary: What a fluent community reviewer confirms for each language before a flyer is printed.
spec: Every fact in the English source appears in this language.
Dates, times, phone numbers and costs match the source exactly.
No words were left in English unless the center chose to keep them, such as a program name.
A fluent community reviewer read the whole flyer and approved it, with the date and flyer version.

artifacts.name: flyer_fact_list
artifacts.title: Flyer Fact List
artifacts.summary: One row per fact and language: the source text, the translated text and whether it matches, changed or is missing.

checklist: Run the fact comparison on the final file that will be printed, not an earlier draft.
A fluent community reviewer approves every language before printing.
Keep each approval with the flyer version it covers.

sources.title: US Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division: Limited English Proficiency
Digital.gov: Plain language guide series

Submitting grant reports or tax filings externally

kit.title: Monthly Program Impact Report Kit
kit.summary: Turns a month of program records into an impact report: totals by measure, change from last month, results against targets, and missing numbers kept as unknown. The program manager checks every figure, and the executive director approves the report and shares it.
kit.target_org: Community nonprofit reporting monthly results to its board and partners

steps.title: Total the month's program records by measure
steps.guidance: Total sessions, people served and outcome check-ins for the month by measure, compare each with the month's target and with last month, and keep any missing count as unknown, never zero.

steps.title: Draft the monthly impact report
steps.guidance: Draft the report's sections: highlights, results against targets, changes from last month, what staff are watching, and next month. Every number comes from the results table, and no participant is quoted without staff approval.

steps.title: Check every figure against the program records
steps.guidance: The program manager traces each figure to the program's own records and corrects or removes any figure that cannot be traced.

steps.title: Approve the report and how shortfalls are explained
steps.guidance: The executive director decides how shortfalls and changes are explained and approves the report.

steps.title: Share the report with the board and partners
steps.guidance: The executive director shares the approved report with the board and partners. The agent never sends or publishes the report.

skills.name: impact-report-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a monthly impact report from a results table, keeping every number traced to a measure and every gap visible.
skills.instructions: Use the outline's sections and word limits: highlights, results against targets, changes from last month, what staff are watching, and next month. Take every number from the results table and cite its measure. Write missing numbers as not yet counted, and name the site they are missing from. Describe what was done and counted in plain words at an eighth-grade reading level, and never claim an outcome the records do not show. Use a participant quote only when staff have marked it approved, never with a name or a detail that could identify the person. Flag every measure below 90 percent of its target for the executive director's explanation.
refuses: Inventing or estimating a missing number
Claiming outcomes the records do not show
Quoting a participant without staff approval
Sharing the report outside the organization

tools.name: summarize_month_by_measure
tools.description: Totals a month's program records by measure and compares each with its target and with last month, listing missing counts as unknown.

artifacts.name: monthly_results_table
artifacts.title: Monthly Results Table
artifacts.summary: One row per measure for the month: target, count, percent of target, last month, change and the record it came from. No participant details.

artifacts.name: impact_report_outline
artifacts.title: Monthly Impact Report Outline
artifacts.summary: Five-section outline for the monthly report, with every number drawn from the results table.
spec: 1. Highlights: three plain sentences, each with its measure.
2. Results against targets, from the results table only.
3. Changes from last month, from the results table only.
4. What staff are watching, written or approved by the program manager.
5. Next month's plans and targets.

checklist: Every number in the report traces to a row in the results table.
Missing counts read as not yet counted, never as zero.
Participant quotes appear only with staff approval and never with a name.
The program manager checks figures before the executive director approves the report.

sources.title: eCFR: 2 CFR 200.329, Monitoring and reporting program performance
National Council of Nonprofits: Administration and Financial Management

kit.title: Food Bank Inventory and Pickup Scheduling Kit
kit.summary: Turns weekly stock counts into a restock and use-first list, and spreads booked pickup slots across volunteer shifts. Household exceptions and every message to households stay with the pantry coordinator.
kit.target_org: Volunteer-run neighborhood food bank with weekly pickup hours

steps.title: Total this week's stock counts and flag items to hand out first
steps.guidance: Add up counts by item and storage area, list items below their restock level, and flag items whose date label falls inside the use-first window for a person to check. Missing counts stay blank, never zero.

steps.title: Spread booked pickup slots across volunteer shifts
steps.guidance: Group booked slots by pickup window, compare them with volunteers per shift, and suggest moving a slot only to a window the household marked as acceptable. Use slot codes, never names.

steps.title: Decide household exceptions, such as extra food or a late pickup
steps.guidance: The coordinator decides any exception for a household in person or by phone, using the pantry's own rules. The agent only lists open requests by slot code.

steps.title: Send pickup reminders and schedule changes to households
steps.guidance: A person reviews the reminder list and sends it from the pantry's own phone or messaging account. The agent never messages households.

skills.name: pickup-plan-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a weekly restock and use-first list and a balanced pickup plan from stock counts and booked slot codes.
skills.instructions: Work only from the stock count sheet and the pickup slot sheet. Total counts per item, list items below their restock level, and mark items whose date label falls inside the use-first window for a person to check; a date label is a prompt for a person, never a ruling on whether food is safe. For pickups, count booked slots per window, compare them with volunteers per shift, and suggest moves only to windows the household marked as acceptable. Use slot codes only, never names, phone numbers or addresses. Leave missing counts blank and list them for the coordinator.
refuses: Deciding which households get extra food or an exception
Messaging or calling households or volunteers
Judging whether food is safe to eat
Storing names, phone numbers or addresses in the plan

tools.name: summarize_stock_and_slots
tools.description: Totals stock counts by item and area, lists items below restock level and inside the use-first window, and counts booked slots per pickup window.

artifacts.name: stock_count_sheet
artifacts.title: Weekly Stock Count Sheet
artifacts.summary: Count sheet by item and storage area, with restock levels and the date label a person checks. No personal data.

artifacts.name: pickup_slot_sheet
artifacts.title: Pickup Slot Sheet
artifacts.summary: Slot codes, pickup windows and the other windows each household said would work, with no names or contact details.

checklist: Count sheets and slot sheets hold codes and counts only; remove any name, phone number or address before the agent reads them.
Check every item flagged to hand out first by hand before moving it to the front shelf.
The coordinator reads the open exception list before any reminder goes out.
Keep missing counts blank so the restock list shows them as unknown.

kit.title: Policy Research Brief Kit
kit.summary: Summarizes a new public rule or ordinance in plain language and cites the clause behind every point, lists dates and who the text says it covers, and marks what the text leaves unclear. What a rule means for the organization or any person, and anything shared publicly, stays with staff.
kit.target_org: Small advocacy and services nonprofit following new city and state rules

steps.title: Number the rule's clauses and pull out dates, definitions and duties
steps.guidance: Number each section and clause as the official text does, and list effective dates, defined terms, who the text says it covers, and duties stated with shall or must, each with its clause number and quoted words.

steps.title: Draft the plain-language brief with a citation for every point
steps.guidance: Write short sections: what changed, who the text says it covers, key dates, what it asks of organizations like ours, and open questions. Every sentence that states what the rule says cites its clause; anything the text leaves unclear becomes an open question, never a guess.

steps.title: Check every citation and quote against the official text
steps.guidance: Confirm each cited clause exists in the official text and each quoted phrase matches it exactly; any mismatch goes back to the brief as an error.

steps.title: Decide what the rule means for the organization
steps.guidance: Staff, with counsel when needed, decide what the rule means for the organization and for the people it serves. The agent never interprets how a rule applies to a person or gives legal advice.

steps.title: Share the brief with staff, partners or the public
steps.guidance: Staff decide whether and how to share the brief or any public statement. The agent never publishes or sends anything.

skills.name: policy-brief-drafter
skills.description: Turns an official rule's text into a plain-language brief that cites a clause for every point.
skills.instructions: Work only from the official text staff provide, with its source link and retrieval date. Number sections and clauses as the official text does. Every sentence that says what the rule says cites a clause, such as Sec. 4(b), and quotes exact words when they matter. Summarize at an eighth-grade reading level. When the text is unclear or two clauses conflict, write an open question instead of a guess. Never say how the rule applies to a particular person, never give legal advice, never write an advocacy position, and mark the brief Not legal advice.
refuses: Saying how a rule applies to a particular person
Giving legal advice
Citing anything except the official text provided
Publishing or sharing the brief

tools.name: index_rule_clauses
tools.description: Numbers the sections and clauses of an official rule text and extracts dates, defined terms and duty sentences with their clause numbers.

artifacts.name: policy_brief_outline
artifacts.title: Policy Brief Outline
artifacts.summary: Five-section outline for a cited plain-language brief, ending with open questions for staff and counsel.
spec: What changed, in two sentences, with clause citations.
Who the text says it covers, quoted.
Key dates: published, effective and any deadlines.
What it asks of organizations like ours, each point with its clause.
Open questions the text leaves unclear, for staff and counsel. Not legal advice.

artifacts.name: clause_citation_log
artifacts.title: Clause Citation Log
artifacts.summary: One row per point in the brief: the sentence, the clause it cites, the quoted words and whether they match the official text.

checklist: Every point in the brief cites a clause in the official text.
Quoted words match the official text exactly, and a different worker checked them.
Anything unclear is an open question, not a guess.
Staff and counsel decide what the rule means for the organization before anything is shared.

sources.title: National Archives: The Federal Register, What It Is and How to Use It
eCFR Reader Aids: Using the eCFR Point-in-Time System
Legal Information Institute (Wex): statute

steps.guidance: The coordinator reviews and sends assignments through the hub's own channels. The agent never messages volunteers.

skills.name: relief-task-matcher
skills.description: Suggests volunteer-to-task matches from skills, availability and recorded training, leaving gaps for the coordinator.
skills.instructions: Use volunteer codes, never names. A volunteer matches a task only when every training the task requires appears in the volunteer's recorded training and the shift fits their availability. Never match anyone marked under 18 to a task the posting marks adults only. Leave a task unmatched rather than stretch a requirement, and list every unmatched task with its reason. Rank only by fit, never by personal traits.
refuses: Placing a volunteer into work that needs training they have not recorded
Giving site safety or medical advice
Messaging volunteers
Ranking volunteers by personal traits

skills.name: shift-briefing-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a one-page site briefing with check-in and check-out steps, tasks and gear lists.
skills.instructions: Write in plain language with short sentences and large headings, printable on one page. Include the meeting point, tasks, required gear, check-in and check-out times and the site lead's role. End with the line: Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. Leave out phone numbers and names; the coordinator adds the site lead's contact.
refuses: Giving safety, medical or structural advice
Adding personal phone numbers or names
Changing a task's training requirements

tools.name: match_volunteers_to_tasks
tools.description: Lists candidate volunteer codes for each task by skill, availability and required training, and lists unmatched tasks with reasons.

artifacts.name: volunteer_roster_template
artifacts.title: Volunteer Roster Template
artifacts.summary: Coded roster with skills, recorded training, available shifts and an adults-only mark. No names or contact details.

artifacts.name: site_shift_briefing
artifacts.title: Relief Site Shift Briefing
artifacts.summary: One-page briefing rules every volunteer hears before a relief shift, with check-in, check-out and the stop-work line.
spec: Check in with the site lead at the meeting point before starting any task.
Work only on the tasks you were assigned; tasks that need training stay with trained volunteers.
Stop work and tell the site lead if anything feels unsafe. The site lead follows local emergency management direction.
Check out with the site lead before you leave, even if you leave early.

checklist: The coordinator confirms every suggested match before assignments go out.
Tasks marked adults only or needing training are never matched without the recorded training.
Briefings carry no personal phone numbers; the coordinator adds the site lead's contact.
The site lead's stop-work call overrides every schedule.

kit.title: Funding Impact Summary for Grant Renewal Kit
kit.summary: Summarizes what a grant paid for and achieved over its whole period for a renewal application: results against the original targets, spending by budget line from the finance lead's figures, and lessons staff name. Missing numbers stay unknown, and staff approve and submit.
kit.target_org: Small community nonprofit applying to renew a two-year foundation grant

steps.title: Compare the grant period's results with the original targets
steps.guidance: Total each measure over the whole grant period, compare it with the original target, and take spending by budget line only from the finance lead's figures. A missing number stays unknown, never zero.

steps.title: Draft the funding impact summary for the renewal
steps.guidance: Draft the renewal's sections: what the grant paid for, results against targets, what it cost by line, what staff learned, and what comes next. Every number comes from the period table, and lessons come only from staff notes.

steps.title: Check every figure against the books and program records
steps.guidance: The finance lead traces every figure to the organization's books and program records and corrects or removes any that cannot be traced.

steps.title: Approve the summary and how shortfalls are explained
steps.guidance: The executive director decides how shortfalls, changes and lessons are explained, and approves the summary.

steps.title: Submit the renewal application to the funder
steps.guidance: The executive director submits the renewal through the funder's own portal. The agent never submits or sends anything.

skills.name: impact-summary-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a grant renewal's funding impact summary from a period results table, keeping every number traceable and every gap visible.
skills.instructions: Use the funder's renewal sections and word limits. Take every number from the period results table and cite its measure or budget line; spending figures are the finance lead's, word for word. Write missing numbers as not yet counted. Describe what the grant paid for and what was done and counted, and never claim a result the table does not show. Take lessons and next steps only from staff notes. Keep participant stories out unless staff supply an approved, de-identified one.
refuses: Inventing or estimating a missing number
Changing the finance lead's spending figures
Claiming results the records do not show
Submitting the renewal

tools.name: compare_period_to_targets
tools.description: Totals each measure across a grant's reporting periods, compares it with the original target, and lists missing numbers as unknown.

artifacts.name: period_results_table
artifacts.title: Grant Period Results Table
artifacts.summary: One row per measure for the whole grant period, with its target, total and percent of target, plus spending by budget line from the finance lead. No participant details.

artifacts.name: renewal_summary_outline
artifacts.title: Funding Impact Summary Outline
artifacts.summary: Five-section outline for a renewal's impact summary, with every number from the period table.
spec: 1. What the grant paid for, by budget line.
2. Results against the original targets.
3. What it cost, from the finance lead's figures.
4. What staff learned, from staff notes.
5. What the next grant period would do.

checklist: Every number traces to the period table, and every spending figure to the finance lead.
Missing numbers read as not yet counted, never as zero.
The finance lead checks figures before the executive director approves the summary.
Only the executive director submits the renewal.

sources.title: eCFR: 2 CFR 200.329, Monitoring and reporting program performance
National Council of Nonprofits: Administration and Financial Management

kit.title: Community Pantry Shift Onboarding & Incident Escalation SOP Pack
kit.summary: Standalone SOP playbook and multilingual role-card drafting skill for volunteer coordinators, reserving all medical, safety, and accommodation decisions strictly for the on-site shift captain.
kit.target_org: Neighborhood mutual-aid pantry and cold-weather shelter

steps.title: Generate printable station checklists and shift handoff notes
steps.guidance: Prepare plain-language station cards (receiving, sorting, distribution, cleanup) with clear escalation contact boxes.

steps.title: Handle accommodation requests and volunteer conduct
steps.guidance: Any conflict or guest accommodation decision is handled in person by the trained shift captain.

steps.title: Execute live medical, weather, or physical safety response
steps.actor: On-site shift captain and certified first-aid lead
steps.guidance: Immediate physical safety or medical distress is handled directly by on-site human responders.

steps.title: Send approved shift schedule and emergency contacts to volunteers
steps.guidance: Coordinator reviews and sends shift packets directly; agents never message volunteers automatically.

skills.name: shift-role-card-drafter
skills.description: Drafts concise, accessible volunteer station cards and shift handoff checklists from a pantry or shelter's operating hours and station list.
skills.instructions: Format each station card at an 8th-grade reading level with three sections: Setup, During Shift, and When to Call the Shift Captain. Never generate medical advice or disciplinary decisions.
refuses: Making volunteer disciplinary or dismissal decisions
Generating clinical or emergency medical instructions
Messaging volunteers or guests directly

artifacts.name: shift_escalation_sop
artifacts.title: Three-Tier On-Site Escalation Playbook
artifacts.summary: Printable escalation tree distinguishing routine supply restocks from immediate human shift-captain and emergency-responder triggers.
spec: Tier 1 (Station Lead): Restock shortages, queue pacing, translation card lookup.
Tier 2 (Human Shift Captain -- immediate): Guest accommodation request, interpersonal dispute, minor facility hazard.
Tier 3 (Human Shift Captain + Local Emergency Services): Medical distress or immediate physical safety concern.

artifacts.name: station_handoff_template
artifacts.title: End-of-Shift Handoff CSV Template
artifacts.summary: Zero-PII station handoff log recording supply counts, equipment status, and open follow-ups for the next coordinator.

checklist: Confirm the on-site shift captain's name and phone extension are filled in before printing station cards.
Verify no guest or volunteer personal health details appear in shift handoff notes.
Walk new volunteers through the Tier 1–3 escalation box during the 5-minute pre-shift huddle.

kit.title: Victim Support Referral Options Kit
kit.summary: Drafts referral options from a public services directory, filtered by service type, language, hours and access needs, and a plain referral checklist for advocates. Every conversation, safety step, decision and contact stays with trained advocates, and nothing in the kit accuses anyone.
kit.target_org: Community victim services program with volunteer advocates

steps.title: Draft referral options from the public services directory
steps.guidance: Filter the public directory by the service types, languages, hours and access needs the advocate enters, show each option's last verified date, and mark entries older than 90 days as verify first. The agent works from service needs only, never from a person's story or location.

steps.title: Draft the referral checklist for the advocate
steps.guidance: List what to confirm with each service before a referral: eligibility in the service's own words, hours, language access, cost, and what the person agreed to share.

steps.title: Hold the support conversation
steps.guidance: A trained advocate talks with the person, listens, and asks what kind of help they want. The agent never talks with the person or reads their story.

steps.title: Do safety planning with the person
steps.guidance: Safety planning happens only between the person and a trained advocate. If anyone is in immediate danger, the advocate follows the program's emergency protocol.

steps.title: Decide and make the referral with the person's consent
steps.guidance: The person decides which options to pursue. The advocate confirms details with the service and shares only what the person agreed to share. The agent never contacts a service about anyone.

skills.name: referral-options-assistant
skills.description: Prepares referral options from a public services directory by service type, language, hours and access needs, with each entry's last verified date.
skills.instructions: Work only from the public services directory and the service needs the advocate enters: service types, languages, hours and access needs. Never read or ask for a person's story, name, contact details or location. Show each option's services, languages, hours, cost, how intake is listed and the date the entry was last verified, and mark entries not verified in the last 90 days as verify first. Use neutral words that describe services and needs, never what happened or who did it. Never rank options by what you think the person should do; the person decides with their advocate.
refuses: Reading or asking for a person's story, name, contact details or location
Deciding which service a person should use
Contacting a service or a person
Describing anyone as responsible for harm

tools.name: filter_service_directory
tools.description: Filters a public services directory by service type, language, hours and access needs, and flags entries not verified recently.

artifacts.name: referral_options_sheet
artifacts.title: Referral Options Sheet
artifacts.summary: One row per matching service from the public directory, with languages, hours, cost, access features, intake as listed and the last verified date. No details about the person.

artifacts.name: referral_checklist
artifacts.title: Referral Checklist for Advocates
artifacts.summary: What an advocate confirms with a service before a referral, ending with the person's choice and consent.
spec: Confirm the service's eligibility in its own words.
Confirm hours and language access, including interpreters.
Confirm cost and how intake works today.
The person decides, and share only what they agreed to share.

checklist: The agent sees service needs only: no names, stories, contact details or locations.
Directory entries marked verify first are confirmed by phone before any referral.
Safety planning and emergencies follow the program's own protocol, with a trained advocate.
Share only what the person agreed to share.

kit.title: Donor Thank-You Letters with Privacy Checks Kit
kit.summary: Drafts thank-you letters from a coded gift list with the acknowledgment details the finance lead requires, and checks that no letter exposes another donor's details or ignores a privacy choice. Staff decide special handling and sign and send every letter.
kit.target_org: Small nonprofit thanking individual donors after a year-end appeal

steps.title: Check the gift list against donors' privacy choices
steps.guidance: Before drafting, check each coded gift row for its anonymous, mail and listing choices, and hold any row with a missing choice for the development lead.

steps.title: Draft a thank-you letter for each gift
steps.guidance: Draft one letter per cleared gift from the approved template with the gift date and amount, the finance lead's acknowledgment wording and a specific line about the program it supports. Names and addresses stay as merge fields.

steps.title: Decide special handling for donors
steps.guidance: The development lead decides personal calls, recognition, anonymity questions and any donor with a missing privacy choice. The agent only lists them.

steps.title: Confirm the gift acknowledgment wording
steps.guidance: The finance lead confirms the receipt wording, including any statement about goods or services given in return, against the organization's own rules and the IRS written acknowledgment requirements.

steps.title: Sign and send each letter
steps.guidance: Staff sign and send letters from the organization's own mail or email. The agent never sends letters or messages donors.

skills.name: donor-letter-drafter
skills.description: Drafts personal thank-you letters from a coded gift list, keeping names and addresses as merge fields.
skills.instructions: Draft one letter per cleared gift row from the approved template. Keep names and addresses as merge fields that the organization's own mail merge fills at signing time, so no letter can carry another donor's details. Include the gift date, the amount and the acknowledgment wording the finance lead supplied, word for word. Add one specific sentence about the program the gift supports from the program notes. Skip any row the privacy check held or that is marked no mail, and list its code. Do not add tax advice.
refuses: Putting one donor's details in another donor's letter or in a shared list
Writing tax advice or changing the acknowledgment wording
Sending letters or messaging donors
Overriding a donor's privacy choice

skills.name: gift-list-privacy-checker
skills.description: Checks a coded gift list for missing privacy choices and rows that must not get a letter or a public listing.
skills.instructions: Check that every row has an anonymous choice, a mail choice and a listing choice. Hold rows with a missing choice for the development lead, and rows with goods or services given in return for the finance lead. Mark anonymous donors so their names stay out of any public list or annual report draft. Report gift codes and counts by choice, never names.
refuses: Guessing a missing privacy choice
Listing an anonymous donor in any public list
Reading or storing names and addresses

tools.name: check_gift_list_privacy
tools.description: Lists gift rows with missing privacy choices, rows marked no mail or anonymous, and rows with goods or services given in return.

artifacts.name: coded_gift_list
artifacts.title: Coded Gift List
artifacts.summary: Gift rows by code with date, amount, program, privacy choices and the value of any goods given in return. Names and addresses stay in the donor system.

artifacts.name: thank_you_letter_template
artifacts.title: Thank-You Letter Template
artifacts.summary: Letter template with merge fields for the donor's name and address, and a place for the finance lead's acknowledgment wording.
spec: Dear {{greeting_name}},
Thank you for your gift of {{amount}} on {{gift_date}} to {{program}}.
One specific sentence about what the program did this year.
The acknowledgment wording supplied by the finance lead, word for word.
Signed by hand by staff.

checklist: Names and addresses stay in the organization's own donor system and enter letters only through its mail merge at signing time.
Every gift row has its anonymous, mail and listing choices before drafting.
The finance lead's acknowledgment wording appears word for word in every letter.
Staff sign and send every letter themselves.

sources.title: IRS: Charitable contributions, written acknowledgments
Association of Fundraising Professionals: The Donor Bill of Rights

kit.title: Handwritten Statements to Text Kit
kit.summary: Types handwritten statements and forms dropped into a folder exactly as written, keeping slang, spelling, acronyms and the writer's own words, and flags every uncertain reading for a person. A local acronym glossary helps readers but never changes the text, and a person checks every flag and signs off.
kit.target_org: Community center that collects handwritten statements and sign-up cards at community nights

steps.title: Type each page exactly as written
steps.guidance: Type each line as written, keeping spelling, slang, grammar, acronyms, crossings-out and line breaks. Mark every unsure reading with [?], mark unreadable words [illegible], and never correct or tidy the writer's words.

steps.title: List acronyms and local terms against the glossary
steps.guidance: List every acronym or local term found, with its glossary meaning when the glossary has one; unknown ones go to the reviewer. The glossary never changes the transcription.

steps.title: Check every flagged reading against the original page
steps.guidance: A person compares every flag and a sample of other lines with the original page, fixes misreadings only, and keeps the writer's own words, spelling and slang.

steps.title: Follow up in person when a statement raises safety
steps.guidance: When a statement mentions danger or not feeling safe, trained staff follow up under the organization's own safety protocol. The agent gives no advice and takes no other step.

steps.title: Sign off the transcription and decide how it is used
steps.guidance: The program lead signs off each transcription and decides how the statement is used, under the organization's consent and records rules.

steps.title: Share a statement outside the organization
steps.guidance: Only staff share a statement outside the organization, and only with the writer's consent. The agent never shares or sends anything.

skills.name: verbatim-transcriber
skills.description: Types handwritten pages exactly as written and flags every uncertain reading for a person.
skills.instructions: Type what is on the page, line by line, exactly as written: keep the writer's spelling, slang, grammar, capital letters, abbreviations, acronyms and punctuation, and write a crossed-out word as [crossed out: word]. Never correct, tidy, translate, summarize or expand anything. When you are not sure of a word, write your best reading followed by [?] and list the alternatives; when you cannot read it at all, write [illegible]. Keep the page and line number for every flag. Never add a name, date or detail that is not on the page. If a page mentions danger or not feeling safe, keep typing it as written and mark the page for trained staff now.
refuses: Correcting spelling, grammar or slang
Summarizing or rewording a statement
Expanding acronyms inside the transcription
Guessing a word without flagging it

skills.name: acronym-glossary-assistant
skills.description: Lists acronyms and local terms in a transcription with their glossary meanings, without changing the text.
skills.instructions: Find acronyms, abbreviations and local terms in the transcription. Give the glossary's meaning, word for word, when the glossary has the term, and list unknown terms for the reviewer to add or explain. Never replace, expand or translate a term inside the transcription; the glossary is a reading aid only.
refuses: Changing the transcription
Guessing the meaning of an unknown local term

tools.name: list_dropped_pages
tools.description: Lists the page images in the intake drop folder with page numbers, sizes and SHA-256 digests, without moving or changing them.

artifacts.name: transcription_rules
artifacts.title: Verbatim Transcription Rules
artifacts.summary: The rules every transcription follows: type exactly what is written, flag what is uncertain, and leave the writer's words alone.
spec: Type exactly what is written: spelling, slang, grammar and acronyms stay as they are.
Write a crossed-out word as [crossed out: word].
Mark an unsure word with [?] and list alternatives; mark an unreadable word [illegible].
A person checks every flag against the original page before anyone uses the text.

artifacts.name: transcription_sheet
artifacts.title: Transcription Sheet
artifacts.summary: One row per written line: the batch, page, line, the text as written, whether it holds a flag, the alternatives and whether a reviewer checked it.

artifacts.name: local_acronym_glossary
artifacts.title: Local Acronym Glossary
artifacts.summary: Acronyms, local terms and common writing abbreviations with their meanings, as a reading aid that never changes a transcription.

rows: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children
General Educational Development, a high school equivalency test
Tuesday Market Center (a SYNTHETIC local term used only in this kit's examples)
Northside Elders Club (a SYNTHETIC local term used only in this kit's examples)
spec.rule: The glossary helps readers. It never changes a transcription.

checklist: Only synthetic or consented pages go in the drop folder; this kit's samples are synthetic, rendered from handwriting fonts and stamped SYNTHETIC.
A person checks every [?] and [illegible] flag against the original page.
Nobody corrects the writer's spelling, slang or wording in the transcription.
Trained staff follow up the same day on any statement about safety.
The program lead signs off before any statement is used or shared.

sources.title: National Archives: Citizen Archivist resources for transcribing records
